user_direction: Keep Protocol's tech decals and UI; keep Reverence darker mood. Push in-world and screen UI toward Wipeout aesthetics. Explore two inbox/environment references as a curveball.

variants.title: Directive
variants.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: one full landscape LCL art-direction study with a raster concept game UI. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET Protocol; Image 2 is a mood/material REFERENCE Reverence, not a new composition. Preserve Protocol's exact fixed elevated three-quarter oblique/trimetric near-parallel camera, framing, hall/piers/stairs/gallery, left shelf and bench, continuous playable floor, four working bowl trays, five people in their same positions and gestures, right technician and tool cart. Keep all four openings and five people readable and uncovered. Keep opaque painted modeled brushwork in the world. Take Reverence's darker blue-grey shadow mood and rich warm ivory/amber/brass light, while retaining Protocol's small green state lenses. The user explicitly likes the machine decals AND the crisp UI as a second style. This is a coherent original LCL graphic identity, with Wipeout-inspired confidence, modular typography, abstract symbols, directional stripes and precise information hierarchy. No copied Wipeout/team logos, racing HUD, lap/speed display, faux Japanese gibberish, neon hologram outlines or global scanline filter. Primary request: combine approved Protocol graphics/UI and Reverence mood, then make the graphic language noticeably MORE ASSERTIVE in both the environment and game HUD. Bold black/ivory typography, coral slash motifs, original civic identity that reads at normal game-view distance. Balance one large emblem and confident bay numbers with fine measured rules and purposeful blank space; still moody, inhabited and legible. Broad dark blue-grey architecture, luminous working amber. UI occupies roughly 12 percent of the whole frame total, restrained to margins. Replace existing modest screen-space cards with a new unified bold screen-space HUD: top-left ivory/coral/slate header 'THE LINE' then 'PROVISION'; upper-right service module 'SERVICE' then 'MANUAL ACCESS'; a low horizontal bottom-edge bay-selection strip showing only '01' '02' '03' '04', with 04 highlighted in coral, and the separate exact phrase 'ALLOCATION ACTIVE'. Keep screen-space UI comfortably inset, crisp flat vector-like with severe sans-serif lettering, asymmetric grid, thick/thin rules, original geometric emblem, deliberate diagonally clipped corners, controlled coral accents and sufficient quiet space. No other wording or tiny pseudo-text. Repeat this graphic family's large original emblem, cut-corner labels, section bars and correctly ordered bay numbers 01,02,03,04 on existing cream machine fascia and pipe collars. Treat these as painted/enamel physical decals, no glowing projected signs. Decals follow perspective and material wear; UI stays clean in screen space. Hardware controls retain purpose. No added objects, people, narrative events, horizon, cinematic lens or floating diorama.
variants.observations: Five people, four trays/bowls and main overhead hall anchors retained. Reverence-like blue-grey stone and local amber light combine with stronger coral machine crests, slash motifs and three large ivory HUD modules. All requested HUD wording and 01–04 strip numbers are legible, with 04 highlighted. Top-left HUD overlaps part of the lamp/pier/stair background; bottom strip covers peripheral floor, but no person or working tray. Machine fascia shows only bay numbers 01–03; pipe labels show 01,02,04, so physical numbering is incomplete. Fine module seams/decals redesigned. UI is more assertive but remains a placard system.

refinement.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. The sole image is the EDIT TARGET Overprint draft. One targeted correction: redesign ONLY screen-space HUD and physical machine decals into a much more angular, modular futuristic graphic-design system. Keep the entire painted hall, exact camera/framing, all five people/poses, four trays/bowls, hardware shapes, palette and lighting unchanged. Current giant ivory placards are too similar to a simple civic poster. Replace them with sparse sophisticated Wipeout-inspired original HUD composition: fine ivory rules and clipped charcoal panels over the world, open negative space, repeated small offset coral bars, a broken-circle emblem paired with three short offset horizontal marks, condensed numbered tab clusters, diagonally notched module edges, deliberate asymmetry. Top-left becomes a compact technical identity cluster, with exact text 'THE LINE' and 'PROVISION', original emblem, one narrow coral identification bar and precise fine dividers. Top-right becomes a slim charcoal/ivory service module with exact text 'SERVICE' and 'MANUAL ACCESS' and a clean wrench pictogram. Bottom UI is separated into several angular dark transparent-looking (but visibly crisp) slate/ivory/coral tabs with exact numbers '01' '02' '03' '04', 04 highlighted strongly; separate right-aligned narrow status block 'ALLOCATION ACTIVE'. Make big numerals contrast with thin technical rules and smaller clear typography. About 15 percent total coverage, no full-width beige banner, no huge background white rectangle. All people, work openings and main routes remain visible. Repeat the same ORIGINAL new broken-circle/offset-bar vocabulary physically on existing cream machine fascia and pipe-collar labels; add bay numbers 01,02,03,04 across the four bays in the correct order. Decals are nonemissive and follow the existing painted perspective/wear; screen UI stays flat crisp vector-like. Avoid copying real Wipeout team identities, racing stats, extra wording/gibberish, neon holograms, excessive crosshairs, glow, scanlines or comic outlines. Retain the dark blue-grey opaque painting exactly. Output one full landscape composition.
refinement.reason: Initial stronger UI converged toward larger civic placards. Test angular modular HUD and a distinct graphic vocabulary while preserving world.
refinement.observations: Final refinement retains five people, four trays and main camera/hall anchors. Angular dark HUD modules, fine ivory rules, separated numbered tabs, coral offsets and broken-ring/three-bar emblem differ clearly from Directive's ivory placards. Required HUD copy and 01–04 tab numbers are legible. All four fascia numbers 01–04 appear; pipe labels remain incomplete. The new emblem and graphic vocabulary replace the prior chevrons, testing identity as well as intensity. Decal placement and fine panel/fitting designs changed; underlying modeled opaque world and warm/cool light remain close, not pixel-identical. HUD overlaps peripheral background/floor but no figures/trays.
